correctness.rationale: The exact objective decrement is (Cx)_i²/2; after a C^(1/2) change of variables the minimax constant is lambda_min(C^(1/2)PC^(1/2)). Concavity in p and swap invariance globally reduce to symmetric p=(u,u,1-2u), not a uniqueness claim for all p. The scaled Hessian decomposes into antisymmetric eigenvalue (1-r)u and the 2x2 symmetric block with smaller eigenvalue ell(u). Its radical discriminant has strictly positive second derivative for c>0, so ell is strictly concave, uniquely maximized at u_s=(1+c)/(3+r+4c). The crossing with the antisymmetric branch occurs at u_b=(r-c²)/(r(3-r)-2c²). Comparing u_s and u_b yields the stated critical quadratic 2c²+(1-r)c-2r=0 and correct two closed-form gamma values. Endpoint gamma=0, C positive definite on stated domain. New independent symbolic identities and 12,500 random-simplex comparisons across 50 parameters passed; numerical tests are not a proof of optimality.

value.rationale: Nonuniform randomized coordinate descent is a natural algorithmic design variable. This two-parameter family is the smallest frustrated Hessian whose inverse cannot be sign-gauged entrywise nonnegative; the exact optimizer has a meaningful active-eigenmode phase boundary despite equal diagonal coordinate curvatures, exceeding generic SDP restatement.

final_claim: For SPD C=[[1,r,c],[r,1,c],[c,c,1]] with 0<r<1 and 0<c<sqrt(r), exact coordinate descent with fixed iid sampling p maximizes sharp one-step worst-case expected energy decrement lambda_min(P^(1/2)CP^(1/2)) at a symmetric law p=(u*,u*,1-2u*). Critical c*=(sqrt((1-r)^2+16r)-(1-r))/4; at c<=c*, u*=(r-c²)/(r(3-r)-2c²), gamma*=(1-r)u*; at c>=c*, u*=(1+c)/(3+r+4c), gamma*=(1+r-2c²)/(3+r+4c). The active bottleneck changes from a mode tie to a single slow symmetric mode.
